events.title: Mikhail Romanov Elected Tsar
events.description: A national assembly, the Zemsky Sobor, unanimously chose the teenage Mikhail Romanov as Tsar of Russia. The choice ended years of turmoil known as the Time of Troubles.
events.significance: His election began the Romanov dynasty, which ruled Russia for more than 300 years, until 1917.

events.title: The Communist Manifesto Is Published
events.description: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels published The Communist Manifesto in London. The pamphlet laid out a materialist view of history and of class struggle.
events.significance: It became one of the most influential political documents ever written, and it shaped revolutionary movements and political debate worldwide.

events.title: First Telephone Directory Issued
events.description: In New Haven, Connecticut, the first telephone directory was issued. It was a single page listing 50 subscribers.
events.significance: It was the start of a way of finding people that lasted for generations, and it showed how fast the telephone was spreading.

events.title: The Battle of Verdun Begins
events.description: Germany opened a massive artillery assault on French positions at Verdun. The fighting became one of the longest and bloodiest battles of World War I.
events.significance: Verdun became a symbol of French resolve and of the huge human cost of trench warfare.

events.title: Malcolm X Is Assassinated
events.description: Malcolm X, the civil rights leader and Black nationalist, was shot and killed at the Audubon Ballroom in New York City while he was about to speak.
events.significance: His death cut short a leading voice of the era. His ideas and his autobiography have kept shaping discussion of race and justice.
